thread:
megan (People Ops): Quick update — USCIS issued an RFE for Tom's H‑1B extension this morning. The RFE asks for detailed client engagement letters and proof of prior wages. This could impact I-9 timing. Need a plan for his 4/1 start.

linda (Hiring Manager): Ugh. We need Tom on the project day 1. Can we onboard him with limited access until his H-1B clears?

natalie (Immigration Counsel): RFE timelines vary. Employers should respond within the timeframe on the notice (usually 87 days). An RFE itself doesn't automatically revoke the petition but USCIS may delay adjudication. For onboarding, options: (1) delay start, (2) bring on as contractor (1099) with no client-facing duties, or (3) hire as W2 contingent on a different status (if available).

tom (Newhire): I don't want to fall behind. I can do advisory work remotely if allowed, but not client on-site. Also worried about benefits start.

finance-bot: Note — contractor onboarding requires completed W-9 + vendor record. Payroll can mirror salary pro-rated for first 30 days but benefits enrollment will be manual and may require a benefits hold.

it-provisioning: For restricted access we can provision a dev VM with no production credentials and block external network for 48 hours while compliance signs off. Requires signed AUP and IT checklist.

megan (People Ops): Proposed hybrid plan: 1) Start date stays 4/1 as "restricted new hire" (no production or client access). 2) Onboarding as 1099 contractor for up to 30 days while RFE is handled; payroll team to issue vendor paperwork. 3) IT to provision dev-only VM and Slack access. 4) Benefits enrollment held until work authorization confirmed.

linda (Hiring Manager): Sounds good. Team can assign onboarding tasks that are internal-only (docs, design reviews, shadowing). I'll update the orientation schedule to exclude any client demos.

natalie (Immigration Counsel): I'll draft a short RFE response packet and a cover memo summarizing recruitment and client letters. Also note: any client letter must avoid implying employer-client relationship that would affect the LCA. I'll DM language templates.

tom (Newhire): Okay to sign AUP and accept contractor letter. Can I get the contractor rate emailed? Need to check taxes.

finance-bot: We'll email the contractor agreement and vendor setup link within 2 business hours. Tom — please complete W-9 and invoice template. Once vendor is active payment runs per our 30-day cycle.

megan (People Ops): Action items and owners:
```
- Natalie: Draft RFE response and template client letters (due in 48 hrs)
- Linda: Redline orientation schedule (today)
- Tom: Complete W-9 + sign AUP (by EOD)
- IT: Provision dev VM + repo access (no prod) (by 4/1)
- Finance: Send contractor packet and hold benefits enrollment until W2 conversion
```

linda (Hiring Manager): I'll also pull prior paystubs and engagement letters we used on contractors; might help Natalie's packet. Dropping links to the folder in #secure.

natalie (Immigration Counsel): Thanks. Once I have the client letters and paystubs I'll finalize the RFE response. If USCIS requests more evidence after our submission, timeline could extend by weeks. I'll keep everyone posted in this thread.

megan (People Ops): Great teamwork. Tom — welcome aboard. We'll treat the first month as a limited-access onboarding and convert you to full W2 once USCIS clears or we confirm alternative authorized status. Ping me with any questions. :slightly_smiling_face:
